doc: Canonical parity schema for flow-dissector parsers. Every dump-meta emitter and the Python comparator (nix/scripts/parity-compare.py) read this file as the single source of truth for: (a) the canonical field name set, (b) the type of each field, and (c) which fields each parser is expected to populate. Adding a field or extending a parser's scope is a contract change tracked here; the parity-gate flake check enforces consistency.

ip_proto.doc: IPv4 protocol or IPv6 next-header byte

ipv4_src.doc: Dotted-quad string; null when addr_type != ipv4

ipv6_src.doc: Lowercase, double-colon-compressed; null when addr_type != ipv6

gre_keyid.doc: GRE key/keepalive ID; doubles as bare keyid in kernel-flowdis

tiers.doc: Reusable scope sets. Each parser's scope is a tier name plus optional per-parser overrides.

tunnel_detection.doc: On packets that contain a tunnel header (the outer parser reports a tunnel-protocol indicator), the inner-flow 5-tuple fields legitimately differ between OUTER-behavior parsers (kernel-flowdis-style) and INNER-behavior parsers (XDP2/xdp2-rs, which follow the tunnel). The comparator masks `inner_outer_fields` when comparing across mismatched tunnel_behavior. This is the structurally-richer XDP2 design — XDP2 reports the actual flow inside the tunnel; kernel-flowdis stops at the tunnel header. See benchmark.c:264-277 and docs/flow-dissector-parity.md 'Phase 17.C findings → Finding 2'.

c-flowdis-usp.doc: Linux kernel userspace flowdis (libflowdis) — bpf_flow_keys equivalent + ARP + TIPC + GRE keyid. Stops at the OUTER 5-tuple on tunnel-encapsulated packets (does NOT follow GRE/VXLAN/Geneve/etc. into the inner flow).

c-xdp2-usp.doc: XDP2 C userspace parser — full FlowMeta-equivalent. Follows tunnels (GRE, IPIP, VXLAN, Geneve, etc.) and reports the INNER 5-tuple. Slower than kernel-flowdis on tunneled traffic, but produces a richer flow signature; see benchmark.c:264-277.

c-xdp2-parse-only.source: Same as c-xdp2-usp; -P flag skips per-packet 200B memset
c-xdp2-parse-only.doc: Identical scope to c-xdp2-usp; perf-only variant

c-xdp2-mono.doc: XDP2 C monolithic single-function parser — R3 architectural-rebuild reference. Same scope as c-xdp2-usp / c-xdp2-parse-only (full FlowMeta + inner-tunnel behavior). Implemented as one function with goto-state transitions instead of a per-node function tree; produces identical metadata to c-xdp2-usp on the covered protocols (30/33 in-tree PCAPs). See xdp2-rs/docs/dispatch-architecture-cost.md §R3.

c-bpf-flowdis.doc: Kernel BPF flow dissector. Same outer-stop behavior as c-flowdis-usp.

c-bpf-xdp2.doc: XDP2 BPF parser. **Verifier-rejected on kernel 7.x** — every record will have accepted=false, reject_reason=verifier

c-bpf-fast.doc: xdp2-flow-ebpf top-N tail-call. Doesn't follow tunnels itself; returns BPF_FLOW_DISSECTOR_CONTINUE on tunnel packets so the kernel's slow path (also outer-only) takes over.

rust-graph.doc: Trait-object dynamic dispatch parser, full FlowMeta. Follows tunnels.

rust-graph-enum.doc: Static-dispatch enum match. Currently table covers Ether/IPv4/{TCP,UDP,ICMP} only — emits reject_reason=ipv4-only on non-IPv4 packets per parity_scope.json:expected_divergences/rust-graph-enum-ipv4-only.

rust-simd.doc: AVX2 batch parser; on non-AVX2 hosts (e.g. Zen 1) every record will have accepted=false, reject_reason=no-avx2

rust-template.doc: Hardware-template fixed-offset extractor. On template miss, accepted=false, reject_reason=no-template (or accept_path=fallback if fall-through to compiled is enabled — TBD in 17.B).

rust-template-simd.doc: AVX2 batch + fixed-offset template; same fallback semantics as rust-template, plus no-avx2 on non-AVX2 hosts

expected_divergences.doc: Kernel BPF verifier rejects flow_dissector.bpf.o on 7.x with 'math between pkt pointer and register with unbounded min value'. Documented Way-5 N/A in docs/flow-dissector-benchmark-plan.md §8.
fast_flow.bpf.c lines 60-79 enumerate the 7 supported chains: ETH/IPv4/{TCP,UDP,ICMP}, ETH/IPv6/{TCP,UDP}, ETH/VLAN/IPv4/{TCP,UDP}. Anything else returns BPF_FLOW_DISSECTOR_CONTINUE.
AVX2 detection at runtime. Zen 1 emits 'warning: AVX2 not available'; xdp2-bench/src/bench.rs maps to N/A.
Template selector returns None when packet shape doesn't match any of the 63 registered templates; rust-template returns Err. The bench.rs template-with-fallback variant is TBD in Phase 17.B.
kernel flowdis and BPF flow_dissector populate bpf_flow_keys, which has no eth_addrs. The comparator masks eth_dst/eth_src when comparing these against full-FlowMeta parsers.
BPF flow dissector path doesn't extract these. They're optional even in kernel-flowdis-usp (only set when packet hit specific paths).

expected_divergences.applies_to: tunnel-encapsulated packets where one parser has tunnel_behavior='outer' and the other has 'inner'
expected_divergences.doc: On packets where the outer parser reports an ip_proto in tunnel_detection.outer_ip_protos OR a UDP dport in tunnel_detection.outer_udp_ports, the comparator masks tunnel_detection.inner_outer_fields between the two behaviors. The XDP2 / xdp2-rs parsers report the INNER 5-tuple by following the tunnel; the kernel-flowdis variants stop at the OUTER 5-tuple. Both are correct under their respective design; XDP2's behavior is structurally richer but slower on tunneled traffic. This is intentional, not a bug. See docs/flow-dissector-parity.md 'Phase 17.C findings → Finding 2'.

rust-graph-enum's enum-dispatch table currently covers Ether/IPv4/{TCP,UDP,ICMP} only (cli.rs:12-13). On packets whose ethertype isn't IPv4 (IPv6, ARP, MPLS, etc.), rust-graph-enum's dump-meta emits reject_reason=ipv4-only. This is a known scope gap (the 2026-05-02 12 ns/pkt headline came from combo.pcap which is IPv4-dominant); extending the enum table to IPv6/VLAN is tracked as a follow-up. Until then, the parity gate treats this rejection as expected.

expected_protocol_acceptance.doc: Per-protocol-template expected acceptance — Phase 3 of the protocol-coverage-matrix plan. Bootstrapped 2026-05-18 from a full 378-pcap run of `nix run .#protocol-coverage-matrix -- --bootstrap-expectations`. Each protocol entry has a 'default' (applied to all parsers) and per-parser 'overrides'. Override vocabulary: 'accept', 'reject:<reject_reason>'. Cells diverging from these expectations are flagged as REJ-unexpected by the aggregator. Known disagreements outside this schema: 4 OK!N cells on icmpv4 (9-10 field disagreements per parser) and vxlan (5-6); both tracked separately as Phase 6 bug-triage. Bench-failed overrides on the rust parsers (e.g. ah, arp, appletalk) reflect packet shapes xdp2-bench doesn't yet handle — REMOVE the override once xdp2-bench is fixed and the cell should become OK. See nix/scripts/protocol-coverage-matrix.py.
